card.name: The word but after a clause
card.fires_on: The contrast word "but" right after a comma that ends a first clause, in general web prose. It also fires on a similar turn like "why" after an opening "if" clause.

modes.label: Comma then but
modes.description: "but" starts a contrasting second clause after a comma.
modes.example: Tuvalu has not developed or grown rich by emitting greenhouse gases,<< but>> is amongst those countries hit hardest by climate

modes.label: But without comma
modes.description: "but" joins two clauses with no comma, still introducing a contrast.
modes.example: Likewise, celebrities don't usually possess any political power<< but>> are familiar to many of the world's

card.plain: It marks the point where a sentence turns to a contrast, as in "X is true, but Y".
evidence: In a recent survey, 97 percent of teens say that texting and driving is dangerous<< but>> 43 percent admit to doing it
Richard Baumert doesn’t have thousands of pigs or calves on feed,<< but>> his feedlots drained the wrong way.
That may be a loaded question,<< but>> it’s hard to talk about affirmative action
